text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed to move in with y.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Deposit(x) ::: x requires a deposit to rent an apartment.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: x has a security deposit of y.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Rent(x, y) ::: x is the monthly rent at y.
RentApartment(x, y) ::: x will rent an apartment in y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(tom, fluffy)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Deposit(oliveGarden) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
Cat(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
Pet(fluffy) ::: Cats are pets.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
(RentApartment(tom, oliveGarden) ↔ (Allowed(tom, fluffy) ∧ SecurityDeposit(tom, y) ≤ 1500)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
(SecurityDeposit(tom, 2000) ∨ ∃y (SecurityDeposit(tom, y) > 2000)) ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
